decision.summary: Neighbour in Flat 3 reported water leaking from Flat 4 onto a light fitting. We created emergency job JOB-101, assigned Swift Plumbing & Heating for an out-of-hours make-safe, messaged the tenant and landlord, and escalated P1 (ESC-106) so an on-call human can authorise key-holder entry. The neighbour was given safety advice and told that damage claims go through the landlord and insurer; the tenant's number was not disclosed.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering the upstairs flat without 24 hours' notice? What conditions apply?
answers.answer: Yes. Active water ingress onto an electrical fitting is an emergency under our safety standard, and it is a genuine emergency, so entry without 24h written notice is allowed. Conditions: entry is limited to making safe (isolate water at the kitchen-sink stopcock, make electrics safe, locate the leak); use the out-of-hours key holder with the contractor; the tenant is informed in writing with what was done; no works beyond make-safe without landlord approval (over £300 inc VAT); keep a photo log. Holding keys does not itself give a right of entry, so a human must authorise it (ESC-106).

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Keep clear of the water and the light fitting, do not touch the fitting, switch off power at the consumer unit if it is safe, call 999 if sparking or burning, and move belongings. An emergency plumber has been booked and the landlord will be informed. Damage claims go to the landlord and their insurer. Do not give the tenant's number or whereabouts, and do not accept liability or promise to pay.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Actions: JOB-101 created (emergency); Swift Plumbing & Heating assigned (C-12); tenant texted (MSG-102); landlord emailed (MSG-103); contractor texted (MSG-104); neighbour call logged (CALL-105); escalated P1 to maintenance (ESC-106). Avoid: admitting fault ('this is your fault' is not accepted); promising to cover the ceiling; giving the tenant's phone number, email, or that she is away; promising a visit time or outcome not confirmed; using legal jargon.
